sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: It's New York City, 1882.
sentences.zh: 那是1882年的纽约市。

sentences.en: At night, this city is mostly dark, but it won't be for long.
sentences.zh: 夜晚的城市大部分时间处于黑暗中，但这种情况不会持续太久。

sentences.en: Thomas Edison has already invented the phonograph, the automatic telegraph,
sentences.zh: 托马斯·爱迪生已经发明了留声机、自动电报机，

sentences.en: and the first commercially viable light bulb.
sentences.zh: 以及第一款具有商业价值的灯泡。

sentences.en: He really could have stopped right there,
sentences.zh: 他本可以就此停步，

sentences.en: but he was still young, only 35 years old.
sentences.zh: 但他当时还很年轻，只有35岁。

sentences.en: And then he had the brilliant idea of doing something even more ambitious.
sentences.zh: 于是他产生了一个更具雄心的天才想法。

sentences.en: He wanted to construct, to design, the electrical system that would supply electricity for those bulbs.
sentences.zh: 他想要建造、设计一套能为这些灯泡供电的电力系统。

sentences.en: That's Philip Shuey.
sentences.zh: 那是菲利普·舒伊。

sentences.en: He wrote The Grid.
sentences.zh: 他写了《电网》一书。

sentences.en: It's a history of how society uses and loses electricity.
sentences.zh: 这是一部关于社会如何使用和失去电力的历史。

sentences.en: The Edison Illuminating Company built a power station in lower Manhattan,
sentences.zh: 爱迪生照明公司在曼哈顿下城建造了一座发电站，

sentences.en: right in the shadow of the newly constructed Brooklyn Bridge.
sentences.zh: 就在刚建成的布鲁克林大桥阴影下。

sentences.en: The first grid was small, about one square mile, and it worked so well that soon all across the country,
sentences.zh: 最初的电网规模很小，大约一平方英里，但运行得非常成功，以至于很快在全国各地，

sentences.en: these little self-contained electrical systems started popping up.
sentences.zh: 这些小型独立电力系统开始涌现。

sentences.en: In the coming 10 and 20, 30 years, the grid got larger and larger.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的10年、20年、30年里，电网变得越来越大。

sentences.en: As the grid grew, it made modern life possible.
sentences.zh: 随着电网的扩张，它让现代生活成为可能。

sentences.en: It powered electric lights, running water, sewage pumps, elevators, and air conditioning.
sentences.zh: 它为电灯、自来水、污水泵、电梯和空调提供了动力。

sentences.en: But the bigger the grid got, the more complicated it got,
sentences.zh: 但电网越大，它就越复杂，

sentences.en: and the more the possibility of failure crept in.
sentences.zh: 故障的可能性也就随之潜入。

sentences.en: Whenever we talk about large, designed, human-made, complicated, electrified things,
sentences.zh: 每当我们谈论大型、经过设计、人造、复杂且电气化的事物时，

sentences.en: it sometimes takes four or five things together going wrong.
sentences.zh: 有时需要四五件事同时出错才会出问题。

sentences.en: But if the system is complicated enough, then the chances of something bad happening go up.
sentences.zh: 但如果系统足够复杂，那么发生坏事的几率就会上升。

sentences.en: Which brings us to New York City's blackout of 1977.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了1977年的纽约市大停电。

sentences.en: It wasn't the first blackout, or even the biggest, but it might have been the most infamous.
sentences.zh: 那不是第一次停电，甚至不是规模最大的一次，但它可能是最臭名昭著的一次。

sentences.en: That's producer Delaney Hall.
sentences.zh: 那是制片人德莱尼·霍尔。

sentences.en: And oh yeah, this story, it's not about Thomas Edison.
sentences.zh: 哦对了，这个故事讲的不是托马斯·爱迪生。

sentences.en: Though it begins with the electrical grid he started building back in 1882.
sentences.zh: 尽管它始于他在1882年开始建造的电网。

sentences.en: A grid that got so big, it's been called the most massive engineering project of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 一个变得如此庞大的电网，以至于被称为20世纪最宏大的工程项目。

sentences.en: This story is about what happens when you disconnect people from that grid.
sentences.zh: 这个故事讲的是当你把人们从那个电网中切断时会发生什么。

sentences.en: For one hot night in New York City.
sentences.zh: 在纽约市一个炎热的夜晚。

sentences.en: It was just time.
sentences.zh: 时候到了。

sentences.en: What we're going to do right here is go back.
sentences.zh: 我们现在要做的就是回顾过去。

sentences.en: It was time for a new way back interpretation.
sentences.zh: 是时候进行一种新的回顾解读了。

sentences.en: Back into time.
sentences.zh: 回到过去。

sentences.en: That's hip-hop pioneer Grandmaster Kaz.
sentences.zh: 那是嘻哈先驱Grandmaster Kaz。

sentences.en: And he says on that night, when the lights went out, a movement was born.
sentences.zh: 他说在那天晚上，当灯光熄灭时，一场运动诞生了。

sentences.en: If I was a kid in the 50s, I'd have been Chuck Berry.
sentences.zh: 如果我是50年代的孩子，我可能会成为查克·贝里。

sentences.en: You know what I'm saying?
sentences.zh: 你知道我在说什么吗？

sentences.en: If I was in the 30s or 40s, I'd have been, you know, a jazz artiSt.
sentences.zh: 如果我生活在30或40年代，我可能会成为一名爵士乐艺术家。

sentences.en: It's the same energy that every generation, you know, exercises.
sentences.zh: 这是每一代人都会展现出的同一种能量。

sentences.en: And it just comes out in different forMs.
sentences.zh: 只是以不同的形式表现出来。

sentences.en: This is Grandmaster Kaz.
sentences.zh: 这就是Grandmaster Kaz。

sentences.en: And yes, I was there during the night of the 1977 New York City blackout.
sentences.zh: 是的，我当时就在1977年纽约大停电的那个晚上。

sentences.en: And survived.
sentences.zh: 并且活了下来。

sentences.en: Thunderstorms swept over the New York City area on a hot night in July.
sentences.zh: 七月的一个炎热夜晚，雷暴席卷了纽约市地区。

sentences.en: What happened in 1977, first of all, you have what, and this might even be the technical
sentences.zh: 1977年发生的事情，首先，你遇到了——这甚至可能是技术上的

sentences.en: word for it, an act of God.
sentences.zh: 术语——天灾。

sentences.en: A lightning bolt came down and struck a overhead transmission line.
sentences.zh: 一道闪电击中了架空输电线。

sentences.en: When lightning adds a bunch of extra electricity to a transmission line, the line shuts itself
sentences.zh: 当闪电给输电线增加了大量额外电力时，线路会在断路器处自动

sentences.en: off at the circuit breaker.
sentences.zh: 切断。

sentences.en: When one line shuts off, the electricity starts squeezing into smaller and smaller channels,
sentences.zh: 当一条线路关闭时，电力开始挤进越来越窄的通道，

sentences.en: like how cars on the freeway crowd into a single lane when the other lanes are blocked.
sentences.zh: 就像高速公路上的汽车在其他车道被堵时挤进单车道一样。

sentences.en: This is all fairly normal so far.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，这一切还算正常。

sentences.en: But then...
sentences.zh: 但随后……

sentences.en: Just 10 or 15 minutes later, another flash of lightning came.
sentences.zh: 仅仅10或15分钟后，又一道闪电劈了下来。

sentences.en: And this knocked out a couple of lines.
sentences.zh: 这又击毁了几条线路。

sentences.en: So now you've got even more electricity with fewer lines to distribute it.
sentences.zh: 所以现在你有更多的电力，却只有更少的线路来分配它。

sentences.en: And it was hot outside, really hot, which meant that lots of New Yorkers were running lots
sentences.zh: 而且外面很热，非常热，这意味着许多纽约人都在使用大量的

sentences.en: of air conditioners, putting an extra burden on the system.
sentences.zh: 空调，给系统增加了额外的负担。

sentences.en: And now they started to have trouble.
sentences.zh: 现在他们开始遇到麻烦了。

sentences.en: There wasn't enough room for all the electricity to flow.
sentences.zh: 没有足够的空间让所有电力流通。

sentences.en: And so Con Edison, that same power company that Thomas Edison started way back when he was
sentences.zh: 于是联合爱迪生公司，也就是托马斯·爱迪生当年在

sentences.en: laying the lines for the first electrical grid...
sentences.zh: 铺设第一条电网线路时创办的那家电力公司……

sentences.en: Started doing the very last thing they like to do, which is to turn off whole neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 开始做他们最不想做的事，那就是关闭整个社区的电力。

sentences.en: One by one.
sentences.zh: 一个接一个。

sentences.en: One by one.
sentences.zh: 一个接一个。

sentences.en: Okay, so the year of the blackout, hip-hop was starting to spread.
sentences.zh: 好吧，停电那年，嘻哈音乐开始传播。

sentences.en: But it was still pretty much a Bronx kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 但它基本上还只是布朗克斯区的一种东西。

sentences.en: It didn't have a name.
sentences.zh: 它当时还没有名字。

sentences.en: You know, people referred to it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们提到它时说。

sentences.en: Oh, y'all still doing that hippity-hoppity stuff.
sentences.zh: 哦，你们还在搞那些嘻嘻哈哈的东西。

sentences.en: Hip-hop, hippity-hop, hip-tida-hop, hip-hop, the hibbidibby hip-hop.
sentences.zh: 嘻哈，嘻嘻哈哈，嘻嘻嗒哈，嘻哈，那种嘻嘻哈哈的嘻哈。

sentences.en: Okay, hip-hop, you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 好吧，嘻哈，你懂我的意思吗？

sentences.en: I do remember what New York was like in that era.
sentences.zh: 我确实记得那个时代的纽约是什么样子。

sentences.en: And I remember how chaotic it was.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时有多混乱。

sentences.en: That's Joe Schloss.
sentences.zh: 那是乔·施洛斯。

sentences.en: I'm a professor at City University of New York, and I research and practice hip-hop culture.
sentences.zh: 我是纽约城市大学的教授，我研究并实践嘻哈文化。

sentences.en: New York City had experienced a major blackout in 1965 in which the city had stayed mostly calm.
sentences.zh: 纽约市在1965年经历过一次大停电，当时城市基本保持了平静。

sentences.en: During the blackout of 1965, residents treated the situation with good humor and camaraderie.
sentences.zh: 在1965年停电期间，居民们以幽默和友爱的心态对待这种情况。

sentences.en: But things felt different in 77.
sentences.zh: 但77年的感觉不同了。

sentences.en: It was like a powder keg.
sentences.zh: 就像一个火药桶。

sentences.en: Like, something like that was on the verge of happening all the time.
sentences.zh: 就像那种事随时都可能发生一样。

sentences.en: All it took was something to push it over the edge.
sentences.zh: 只需要一点推力就能让它爆发。

sentences.en: A couple years before, in 1975, New York City was in such a dire financial situation
sentences.zh: 几年前的1975年，纽约市处于极其严重的财政困境中，

sentences.en: that it had turned the federal government for a bailout.
sentences.zh: 以至于它向联邦政府寻求救助。

sentences.en: President Gerald Ford's response was a resounding no,
sentences.zh: 杰拉尔德·福特总统的回答是响亮的拒绝，

sentences.en: prompting the New York Daily News to run a now-famous headline,
sentences.zh: 促使《纽约每日新闻》刊登了现在著名的头条新闻，

sentences.en: Ford to City, Drop Dead.
sentences.zh: 福特对城市说：去死吧。

sentences.en: In 1977, things were still bad for New York.
sentences.zh: 1977年，纽约的情况依然糟糕。

sentences.en: And in the Bronx, they were even worse.
sentences.zh: 而在布朗克斯区，情况更糟。

sentences.en: You had neighborhoods that had lost something like 46% of the population.
sentences.zh: 有些社区失去了大约46%的人口。

sentences.en: My name is Lloyd Altan, and I am the Bronx Borough Historian.
sentences.zh: 我叫劳埃德·阿尔坦，我是布朗克斯区历史学家。

sentences.en: And there were blocks after block after block of rubble.
sentences.zh: 那里有成片成片的废墟。

sentences.en: And beyond that, what was on the horizon were buildings that were empty and boarded up.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，地平线上是空置并用木板封住的建筑物。

sentences.en: Really, it looked like Berlin right after the bombings in World War II.
sentences.zh: 真的，看起来就像二战轰炸后的柏林。

sentences.en: The municipal government had forgotten about the Bronx.
sentences.zh: 市政府已经遗忘了布朗克斯。

sentences.en: And then the youth in the Bronx had been forgotten about by the older people in the Bronx.
sentences.zh: 而布朗克斯的年轻人也被布朗克斯的老年人遗忘了。

sentences.en: We didn't have those music prograMs.
sentences.zh: 我们没有那些音乐项目。

sentences.en: All those were cut out.
sentences.zh: 那些全都被砍掉了。

sentences.en: When we were kids, you know, we had them.
sentences.zh: 当我们还是孩子的时候，你知道，我们有这些项目。

sentences.en: But those intermediate years, it's like, we didn't have none of that anymore.
sentences.zh: 但在那中间的几年里，就像是，我们什么都没有了。

sentences.en: So they were like a forgotten minority of a forgotten minority of a forgotten minority.
sentences.zh: 所以他们就像是被遗忘的少数群体中的少数群体，再少数群体。

sentences.en: So, I mean, you can really see how people could feel that they had been left behind.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，你真的能看出人们为什么会觉得他们被抛弃了。

sentences.en: I mean, it's hard to describe, you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很难描述，你懂我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Because now that we're older, I can look back and say, wow, we got through some pretty rough times.
sentences.zh: 因为现在我们长大了，我可以回过头来说，哇，我们经历了一些非常艰难的时期。

sentences.en: You know, but rough, if you were born into rough times, then it's just times.
sentences.zh: 你知道，但艰难，如果你出生在艰难时期，那它就只是生活。

sentences.en: You know, we got through some pretty rough times.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们经历了一些非常艰难的时期。

sentences.en: You know, we got through some pretty rough times.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们经历了一些非常艰难的时期。

sentences.en: You know, we got through some pretty rough times.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们经历了一些非常艰难的时期。

sentences.en: You know, we got through some pretty rough times.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们经历了一些非常艰难的时期。

sentences.en: So, again, my friend, the funky beat has no end.
sentences.zh: 所以，再说一次，我的朋友，时髦的节拍永无止境。

sentences.en: We about to take you on down to the AM for you and your friend.
sentences.zh: 我们正要带你进入AM电台，为你和你的朋友。

sentences.en: Because the sounds you hear is kind of tough on your ear.
sentences.zh: 因为你听到的声音对你的耳朵来说有点刺耳。

sentences.en: Coming at you so loud and clear, so you have no fear.
sentences.zh: 声音响亮而清晰地传向你，所以你不用害怕。

sentences.en: On the evening of July 13th, 1977, the same day as the blackout, Grandmaster Kaz and his partner Disco Wiz
sentences.zh: 1977年7月13日晚上，也就是停电的那天，Grandmaster Kaz和他的搭档Disco Wiz

sentences.en: had been challenged to a DJ battle by another group of DJs.
sentences.zh: 被另一群DJ挑战进行DJ对决。

sentences.en: So we decided to take our equipment out into the park.
sentences.zh: 所以我们决定把设备带到公园里。

sentences.en: We used to hang out, play basketball in every day.
sentences.zh: 我们过去每天都在那里闲逛、打篮球。

sentences.en: So that's where the battle was going to take place.
sentences.zh: 所以对决就在那里进行。

sentences.en: They set up all their stuff side by side.
sentences.zh: 他们把所有的东西并排摆放好。

sentences.en: I just remember them having a very, very good professional sound system
sentences.zh: 我只记得他们有一套非常、非常好的专业音响系统，

sentences.en: and us having our thrown together, you know, in pieces set.
sentences.zh: 而我们的是拼凑起来的，你知道，零散的设备。

sentences.en: The two groups of DJs started to battle.
sentences.zh: 两组DJ开始对决。

sentences.en: I was doing this little combo that I used to do.
sentences.zh: 我当时正在做我常用的那个小组合动作。

sentences.en: And one song was a song by D.C.
sentences.zh: 其中一首歌是D.C. LaRue的歌。

sentences.en: LaRue.
sentences.zh: 我用另一个破碎节拍把它切入。

sentences.en: And I would cut it up with this other break beat.
sentences.zh: 咚咚，咚咚咚咚咚。

sentences.en: Dun-dun, dun-dun-dun-dun-dun.
sentences.zh: 啊，爱，爱，爱。

sentences.en: Ah, love, love, love.
sentences.zh: 我当时表现得太棒了。

sentences.en: And I was killing them.
sentences.zh: 现在，记住这一点，每个人都非常兴奋。

sentences.en: Now, remember that, the hype of everybody, you know, being really excited.
sentences.zh: 然后唱片就开始变慢了。

sentences.en: And then the record just started slowing down.
sentences.zh: 你懂我的意思吗？

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 就是，你知道，你知道唱机是怎么停下来的，然后就是，

sentences.en: Just, you know, you know how turntable cuts off and then just,
sentences.zh: 噢，那种情况。

sentences.en: ooh, that kind of situation.
sentences.zh: 所以很自然地，我们以为是我们自己的问题。

sentences.en: So quite naturally, we thought it was us.
sentences.zh: 我们以为我们消耗了太多的电力，

sentences.en: We thought we had drained too much power
sentences.zh: 导致电力短路了。

sentences.en: and we shorted out, you know, the electricity.
sentences.zh: 所以我们很慌乱。

sentences.en: So we're frantic.
sentences.zh: 我们四处张望。

sentences.en: We're looking around.
sentences.zh: 我们检查按钮。

sentences.en: We're checking buttons.
sentences.zh: 我们检查开关。

sentences.en: We're checking switches.
sentences.zh: 我们看看发生了什么。

sentences.en: We're seeing what's up.
sentences.zh: 因为在对决中如果系统坏掉，

sentences.en: Because this is death in a battle
sentences.zh: 那就是死路一条。

sentences.en: if your system conks out on you.
sentences.zh: 但过了一会儿，我们周围的一切开始变暗。

sentences.en: But after a while, everything around us started getting dark.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，窗户，我们周围的公寓楼全都黑了。

sentences.en: I mean, windows, the apartment buildings around us were all dark.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，窗户，我们周围的公寓楼全都黑了。

sentences.en: It kind of came over everybody at the same time.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉似乎同时笼罩了所有人。

sentences.en: Like, oh, blackout.
sentences.zh: 就像是，噢，停电了。

sentences.en: Generators all over the city had been turning themselves off one by one.
sentences.zh: 城里各处的发电机一台接一台地自动关闭了。

sentences.en: And then the biggest generator in the city.
sentences.zh: 然后是城里最大的那台发电机。

sentences.en: A machine called Big Alice.
sentences.zh: 一台叫“大爱丽丝”的机器。

sentences.en: It turned itself off.
sentences.zh: 它也自动关闭了。

sentences.en: And with that, just about everything left
sentences.zh: 随着它的关闭，纽约城里几乎所有

sentences.en: that was still lit up in New York turned off.
sentences.zh: 还亮着的灯光也都熄灭了。

sentences.en: All five boroughs of New York City went dark.
sentences.zh: 纽约市的全部五个行政区陷入了一片黑暗。

sentences.en: But if you turn all those fluorescent lights off,
sentences.zh: 但如果你关掉所有那些荧光灯，

sentences.en: that glow, that diffused light goes away
sentences.zh: 那种光晕，那种弥散的光线就会消失，

sentences.en: and you can look up, pow, there it is, the Milky Way.
sentences.zh: 然后你抬头看，砰，就在那儿，银河。

sentences.en: If people took a minute to gaze up at the newly visible night sky,
sentences.zh: 如果人们花点时间抬头凝望那片新显现出来的夜空，

sentences.en: they didn't stargaze for long.
sentences.zh: 他们也不会看太久。

sentences.en: Because pretty soon, things started to feel tense.
sentences.zh: 因为很快，气氛就开始变得紧张起来。

sentences.en: The stores started to close.
sentences.zh: 商店开始关门了。
